baseline_models.focus_anchor: The question about seeing is attached to creating, intentional work, hands, and the resulting livestock.
baseline_models.mechanism: Perceptual and reflective seeing is directed toward a production chain: prior measure, origination, purposive work, and concentrated agency yield an ordinary visible herd.

activation_trace.role: Eye-and-insight seeing makes the herd an inspectable piece of evidence.
Prior measuring supplies the design stage of the production mechanism.
Origination supplies the transition from measured possibility to living creatures.
Purposive action marks the making as intended rather than accidental.
Attribution of action to hands concentrates authorship and responsibility for the work.

changed_reading.before: People merely notice that livestock exist among their possessions.
changed_reading.after: The familiar herd is an exposed signature of measured, purposive divine making that demands an inference from sight.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The benefactive 'for them,' livestock, divine hands, and the final human ownership clause form a transfer sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: The hand can carry favor and control, livestock can carry both animal wealth and good condition, and ownership names the limited human endpoint of a gift whose source remains outside the owners.

activation_trace.role: The hand-as-favor image casts the act of making as benefaction toward the recipients.
The possessing hand anticipates the transfer from divine production to human control.
Animal wealth fixes the concrete object transferred into human possession.
Good condition and bestowed favor remain audible behind the livestock category.
Property and disposal rights identify the human endpoint without erasing the prior giver.

changed_reading.before: The closing clause reports a neutral fact of livestock ownership.
changed_reading.after: Human property is a bestowed layer of control: the owners receive animal wealth but do not originate its life or their title to it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opening interrogative asks observers to account for the livestock they already treat as unremarkable property.
baseline_models.mechanism: The seeing root moves from perception through reflection to an attention-demanding inquiry, turning normalized possession into the very datum that should unsettle the possessor.

activation_trace.role: Reflective opinion converts visual familiarity into deliberation about cause.
The attention-and-inquiry image makes the question a demand for an account, not a request for eyesight.
Actual possession supplies the normalized fact on which the inquiry turns.

changed_reading.before: The question asks whether they have physically observed cattle.
changed_reading.after: The question asks why sustained ownership has failed to become reflective recognition of the source of that ownership.

context_deltas.mechanism: The revived-earth sequence marks food as a visible sign, places fruit beside a human-hand clause, and ends in gratitude; the livestock sequence repeats work and hands, then names uses, drinks, and the same gratitude question. The focus therefore sits inside a repeated audit of source, human use, and response.

activation_trace.role: A manifest sign establishes provisioning as evidence meant to be read.
Purposive human work supplies the comparison point for the focus's divine work.
Hand-attributed action makes workmanship and its limits the issue in the fruit sequence.
Recognition of favor names the required response to received produce.
The focus relocates hand-attributed making explicitly to divine agency.
The favor image lets the animal category carry the value being acknowledged.
Benefit translates the created herd into experienced human advantage.
Edible-and-drinkable wealth makes the herd a stored provisioning system.
The abundance-and-milk image makes gratitude materially legible in animal yield.

structural_cues: 36:33-35 and 36:71-73 are parallel provisioning sequences, each moving from a supplied source to consumption and ending with the same gratitude question.
The work-plus-hands pairing recurs at 36:35 and 36:71 with different agents.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated sign, work, hands, use, and gratitude sequence; I infer that the repetition distinguishes derivative human use from ultimate origination. A live alternative is simple thematic reinforcement without a deliberate agency contrast.

changed_reading.before: The focus is a standalone creation proof based on livestock.
changed_reading.after: The focus is the second movement of a provisioning audit: human work can handle a yield, but the living source and the capacity to benefit remain gifts that call for gratitude.

context_deltas.mechanism: A laden vessel carries descendants, comparable rideable means are created, and continued passage is mercy for a term; the animals are then made tractable for riding. Livestock possession becomes one terrestrial component of a wider created transport and survival network.

activation_trace.role: The carrier-or-mount image establishes conveyance as a supplied instrument.
Created comparable means extend conveyance beyond the single laden vessel.
Literal riding identifies mobility as the practical output.
Merciful tenderness frames continued transport and survival as granted rather than secured.
Livestock supplies the concrete terrestrial carrier and food stock.
Possession gives humans practical access to the created transport resource.
Making a difficult creature tractable explains how created life becomes usable mobility.
Riding confirms that part of the herd functions as transport.

structural_cues: 36:41-44 moves from carriage to comparable rideable creations, possible drowning, and time-limited mercy.
36:71-72 repeats creation for them and immediately specifies tractability, riding, and eating.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel carriage, creation-for-them, riding, vulnerability, mercy, and subdued animals; I infer one transport ecology linking vessel and herd. A live alternative is that 36:42 refers only to further vessels, though 36:72 independently secures the livestock-mobility link.

changed_reading.before: The owned herd is primarily a static food asset.
changed_reading.after: The herd is a created, tractable carrier within a mercy-dependent infrastructure for movement, continuity, and food.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command to spend from divinely allotted provision and to feed others supplies a social direction for the focus's transfer of animal wealth into human ownership: what is made for them is not thereby sealed off within them.

activation_trace.role: The going-out of wealth turns possession into an outward material flow.
Allotted gift identifies owned resources as prior provision rather than self-grounded acquisition.
Feeding another supplies the interpersonal destination of provision.
The divine hand as favor identifies the herd as something first given.
Animal wealth supplies a concrete stock from which food and value can circulate.
Human disposal rights create the capacity, and therefore the practical site, for sharing.

structural_cues: 36:47 rejects the claim that divine ability to feed cancels the human duty to feed from divine provision.
The focus repeats the benefactive 'for them' before naming them owners.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies allotted provision, commanded expenditure, feeding, bestowed livestock, and ownership; I infer that received control carries distributive responsibility. A live alternative limits the focus to gratitude and treats the feeding duty as a separate social episode.

changed_reading.before: Ownership grants the beneficiaries private use of animal wealth.
changed_reading.after: Ownership appoints them as active holders of prior provision, with enough control to let its food and value move toward others.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated seeing-and-creation question turns from livestock to the human observer, then recalls the observer's drop-origin, forgotten creation, and first origination. The subject who looked outward as owner is forced back inside the same category of made, dependent life.

activation_trace.role: Seeing initially positions humans as observers of created livestock.
Origination marks the herd as made life.
Property places humans above the herd within the local social relation.
The renewed attention-question redirects inquiry from the owned creature to the owner.
The same originating agency now governs the human observer.
A minute generative fluid undercuts the owner's posture of autonomous mastery.
Loss of remembered origin explains why visible possession failed to yield recognition.
First bringing-into-being closes the inversion by locating both owner and owned under origination.

structural_cues: 36:71 and 36:77 repeat the same opening attention-question and the clause that divine agency created the object under review.
36:78 explicitly says the human forgot his own creation before 36:79 invokes first origination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated syntax and the shift from livestock creation to human creation; I infer a reversal of observer and observed that relativizes ownership. A live alternative treats the two questions as cumulative but independent proofs.

changed_reading.before: Humans stand outside the created herd as its settled owners.
changed_reading.after: The owner is only locally above the herd: he too is made from vulnerable material and remains dependent on the same originating agency.

context_deltas.mechanism: Human hands testify to what humans acquired, divine hands make the herd humans possess, and the closing hand contains dominion over everything. The repeated hand and ownership terms nest human property between accountable action and comprehensive divine rule.

activation_trace.role: Hands bear attributed deeds and can expose rather than secure their human possessor.
Knowledge-bearing testimony makes human agency answerable.
Acquiring benefit links ordinary gain and property to the record of action.
Divine hands occupy the originating side of the focus's agency chain.
Human property is the intermediate, local layer of control.
The possessing-hand image gathers every subordinate title inside a final possessor.
Comprehensive sovereignty supplies the outer boundary around human ownership.

structural_cues: 36:65 makes body parts witnesses against their users, while 36:83 closes with hand, dominion over every thing, and return.
The focus places divine hand-work and human ownership between those two scenes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hand-attributed deeds, testimony, divine hand-work, human property, total dominion, and return; I infer a hierarchy of accountable agency. A live alternative reads the hand scenes separately without making ownership their connecting axis.

changed_reading.before: The final phrase gives humans an uncomplicated title over livestock.
changed_reading.after: Their title is real but nested and reviewable: their own hands answer for acquisition while all possession remains inside comprehensive dominion.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the water-logistics branch of ownership and the milk-abundance branch of gratitude, neither of which is the default lexical rendering. It remains anchored in livestock, possession, benefits, drinks, and the immediate gratitude question. Downstream prose should present it as an exploratory material analogy, not as a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Livestock are owned, then immediately described as sources of benefits, drinks, and gratitude.

activation_trace.role: Animal wealth supplies the living store from which survival goods emerge.
Water that lets travelers command their situation recasts ownership as practical survival capacity.
Wealth that can be eaten and drunk identifies the herd as consumable capital.
Abundance expressed through plentiful milk gives the gratitude appeal an animal-specific yield.

changed_reading.before: Livestock ownership is an abstract property relation followed by generic benefits.
changed_reading.after: The herd is portable survival capacity: living wealth converted into drink and nourishment, with productive abundance answering to gratitude.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links the animal-leader branch of ownership and the camel-hobbling branch of reason to worship and subdued livestock. It remains anchored in explicit livestock, ownership, tractability, and the nearby demand to reason and obey. Downstream prose should mark the self-restraint analogy as reader-supplied and avoid claiming that the context words lexically mean herd management here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Humans are called owners of livestock that are then made tractable for them.

activation_trace.role: The explicit herd keeps the analogy attached to actual managed animals.
The leading animal or guide image turns bare ownership toward direction of a following group.
Submissive obedience supplies the response demanded of the human owners.
Hobbling a camel supplies a concrete image of restraint behind the failed exercise of reason.
Tractability after difficulty makes animal compliance visible to its human beneficiary.

changed_reading.before: Owners exercise control over compliant animals.
changed_reading.after: Their managed herd becomes an ironic mirror: people capable of restraining and directing animals fail to restrain themselves into the obedience and straight course asked of them.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the camel-conception branch of origination in the resurrection argument. It remains anchored by the focus's created livestock and the later sequence of drop-origin, forgotten creation, and first bringing-into-being. Downstream prose should render it as a small-scale biological analogy for origination, not restrict the later verse to camel pregnancy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus presents living livestock as the outcome of divine creation rather than as inert manufactured stock.

activation_trace.role: Origination identifies the herd as repeatedly living created matter.
Concrete livestock gives the later gestational image an anchor in the focus.
Generative fluid supplies the human instance of life emerging from slight material.
Camel conception and visible pregnancy provide an animal-scale image of life beginning and rising into view.

changed_reading.before: The livestock stand as finished objects already made for human use.
changed_reading.after: The living herd also displays recurring gestational origination, a nearby biological micro-model for the later claim that first creation grounds renewed life.

strongest_changes: The repeated work-hands-use-gratitude sequence turns the herd into an agency audit rather than an isolated creation example.
The spending and feeding scene changes possession from private benefit into control over provision that can circulate.
The repeated creation question and the closing dominion scene place the human owner back among created, accountable, subordinate beings.
summary.what_was_special: The focus compresses seeing, creation, purposive work, hands, animal favor, and ownership into one chain; whole-surah repetitions then reverse that chain by contrasting human and divine hands, owner and creature, local property and total dominion.
remaining_uncertainties: The human-hand clause at 36:35 permits more than one syntactic relation to the fruit, so the retained model relies on the explicit recurrence without forcing that ambiguity.
The exact referent of the comparable rideable creation at 36:42 remains broad, although 36:72 independently anchors livestock transport.
The water-capacity, herd-leader, camel-hobbling, milk-abundance, and gestation activations are branch-distant and should remain explicitly exploratory.
